# Commonplace Plugins

Commonplace Plugins is Cooper Corbett's private marketplace for reusable
personal workflows, software development, interface design and animation in
Codex and Claude Code.

## Choose your plugins

Start with `foundations` for personal work. Add `development-workflows` for
software repositories, interface design and animation.

| Plugin                  | What it provides                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `foundations`           | Writing, visualisation, personal email, Instapaper and household finance workflows. |
| `development-workflows` | Repository work, product requirements, interface design and animation.              |

### Included skills

`foundations` provides the five personal skills:

- `instapaper-article-save`
- `voice`
- `data-visualisation`
- `personal-email-triage`
- `home-finance-audit`

`development-workflows` provides:

- `repo-structure`
- `package-structure`
- `docs-maintainer`
- `strict-effect-ts`
- `effect-client-wrapper`
- `alchemy-iac`
- `prd-writer`
- `prd-review`
- `prd-implementer`
- `linear` for project issues, dependencies, related work and release updates

It also includes seven unchanged Matt Pocock skills:

- `grill-me`
- `grilling`
- `grill-with-docs`
- `improve-codebase-architecture`
- `codebase-design`
- `domain-modeling`
- `setup-matt-pocock-skills`

It also provides 20 interface design skills and 15 animation skills. The shared
`prototype` skill appears once:

- Interface design: `animations`, `ask-emil`, `ask-lapse`, `build-a-tool`,
  `color`, `component-design`, `design-foundations`, `design-vocabulary`,
  `engineering-vocabulary`, `forms-and-inputs`, `get-creative`,
  `marketing-pages`, `performance`, `prototype`, `surfaces`,
  `touch-and-accessibility`, `typography`, `ui-polish`, `ui-review`,
  `writing-skills`
- Animation: `animate`, `animation-accessibility`, `animation-performance`,
  `animation-vocabulary`, `css-animations`, `debug-animation`,
  `emil-design-engineering`, `find-animation-opportunities`, `gesture-ui`,
  `improve-animations`, `motion-brief`, `motion-react`, `pick-ui-library`,
  `review-animations`, `scroll-animations`

The Instapaper skill uses the connected Executor (Personal) app. Instapaper credentials
remain in Executor and are not stored in this repository.

## Install in Codex

You need access to Cooper's private GitHub repository.

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add crcorbett/commonplace-plugins --ref stable
codex plugin add foundations@commonplace
codex plugin add development-workflows@commonplace
```

Start a new Codex task after installation so Codex loads the plugin and skills.

### Use a skill in Codex

Type `$`, select a skill such as `foundations:voice` or
`development-workflows:repo-structure`, then write your request. You can also
ask in plain language and let Codex choose a matching skill.

## Install in Claude

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add 'https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins.git#stable'
claude plugin install foundations@commonplace
claude plugin install development-workflows@commonplace
```

Start a new Claude Code session after installation. Claude can use the skill's
instructions, but the Executor app route is specific to supported OpenAI
surfaces.

## Optional companion: Impeccable

[Impeccable](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable) is maintained upstream, so
install it separately. This keeps one up-to-date copy for each client instead
of copying its files into Commonplace.

In Claude Code, add its marketplace, then open `/plugin` and install
Impeccable:

```text
/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable
```

For Codex, run the upstream installer from a project folder. Choose global
scope if you want the skill available in every project:

```bash
npx impeccable install --providers=codex --scope=global
```

Codex may ask you to approve Impeccable's project hook in `/hooks`.

Replace `Vary: Cookie` appearance variants with a TanStack `ScriptOnce` theme script that applies the saved choice before first paint, and check both variant orders in hosted cache proof.

TanStack manages route loading, serialisation and freshness, while component query Atoms share the existing runtime factory and registry.

Preserve complete request deadlines, cancellation and checked reply variants. Qualify server rendering, hydration, public request origins and matching deployment stages. Use native Alchemy version-scoped caching for eligible public responses and prove cache hits and fresh JSON/HTML after content deployment; optional procedure and streaming RPC remains available.

# Documentation

There is no active implementation plan.

- [Repository guide](../README.md)
- [Architecture](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Release and client refresh runbook](runbooks/release.md)
- [Foundations skill source register](../plugins/foundations/sources.json)
- [Development Workflows skill source register](../plugins/development-workflows/sources.json)
- [Documentation ownership map](documentation-map.json)

Local template qualification is retained in [the evidence archive](archive/README.md).
# Release and client refresh

This repository releases two private plugins and publishes nothing to npm.

## Prepare a change

1. Update the canonical skill under `plugins/foundations/skills` or
   `plugins/development-workflows/skills`, or update the plugin metadata.
2. Update the relevant source review date when approved skill content changes.
3. Refresh both checked `sources.json` fingerprints with `bun run source:sync`.
   Only a register whose packaged skill files changed will be rewritten.
4. Run `bun run changeset` and select the changed plugin package.
5. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run test` and
   `bun run verification`.
6. Review the complete Git-tracked distribution report before pushing.

Write the Changeset for maintainers: describe the concrete engineering change,
affected plugin and any compatibility or migration details. Changesets owns the
generated `plugins/<plugin>/CHANGELOG.md` entry. Review it in the Version
Packages pull request; preserve earlier entries and do not hand-write a
published version before the version step runs.

When repository or package templates change, render a fresh repository and
install its pinned dependencies. Finalise the render receipt with
`repo-structure/scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py`, then run the generated
repository's full `bun run verification`. Repeat its package build to check that
removing compiled files also removes TypeScript's saved build record. Run the
repository validator's adversarial cases as well: restoring a TanStack backend
route, source import or Effect Context bridge must fail. Keep these local results
separate from any deployment or real browser evidence.

## Release

After a Changeset reaches `main`, GitHub Actions opens or updates the Version
Packages pull request. Merging it synchronises manifests, reruns verification,
creates a tag and private GitHub release for each new plugin version. It advances
`stable` only when a new plugin tag points to that exact commit. An unrelated
`main` update does not move the client branch.

After release, read back `main`, `stable`, each new tag and each GitHub release.
New tags must resolve to the release commit. `stable` must resolve to the
complete marketplace commit. Fix a released error with a new patch version
instead of rewriting a tag.

### When GitHub Actions cannot start

If job annotations confirm that account usage, payment, spending or runner
limits prevented execution, run the existing checks and release steps locally.
Keep a build or test failure separate: it must still be fixed. Record the
blocked run and local results in the relevant pull request. Use normal merge
permissions; local results do not change GitHub's required checks automatically.

1. Use the pinned Bun version, install with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`,
   then run `bun run test` and `bun run verification` on the exact change.
2. Merge the checked Changeset pull request and update the local `main` checkout.
3. Create a release branch and run `bun run version-packages`. This consumes
   Changesets, generates changelogs and manifests, and runs tests and verification.
4. Review the version changes, commit them and open the Version Packages pull
   request. Merge it after the same local checks pass.
5. Update to the exact merged `main` commit, install frozen dependencies and
   rerun both local checks. Confirm no automated release job is active.
6. Run `bun run release`, then push only each newly created plugin tag. Create
   its private GitHub release with `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag
--generate-notes --title <title>` after checking it points at that commit.
7. Read back each new tag and release before advancing `stable` to the exact
   release commit. Read back `main` and `stable` as described above.

Preserve existing tags, releases and workflow checks. This local route uses the
same Changesets and manifest commands as CI and publishes nothing to npm.

## Connect the release to Linear

For work tracked in Linear, use the canonical
[Linear release guidance](../../plugins/development-workflows/skills/linear/references/development-and-release.md).
The repository changelog records engineering details. Linear project updates
explain the product result, availability and any action users need to take.

Before closing the delivery issue, read the published changelog at the release
commit and check its package, version and PR/issue links. Record the changelog,
tag/release, checks and remaining rollout work on the issue. Publish one useful
product update for the project's released version or shared release group,
linking the exact changelog entry, release and affected issues. Reuse or correct
an existing update for that release so retries do not create another copy.
Keep a pending release or unverified live rollout clearly labelled as pending.

## Refresh Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add crcorbett/commonplace-plugins --ref stable
codex plugin add foundations@commonplace
codex plugin add development-workflows@commonplace
```

Start a new task after installation. Marketplace visibility does not prove
that an already-open task loaded the new skill.

## Refresh Claude

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add 'https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins.git#stable'
claude plugin install foundations@commonplace
claude plugin install development-workflows@commonplace
```

Reload plugins or start a new session. Claude can load the workflow
instructions, but the Executor app integration is available only on supported
OpenAI surfaces.

## Refresh vendored schemas

Use `bun run schema:refresh` only when deliberately reviewing an upstream
schema update. Review the downloaded files, then run the full tests and
verification before committing them.

1	# Cloudflare
2	
3	## Contents
4	
5	- [Ownership decisions](#ownership-decisions)
6	- [File ownership](#file-ownership)
7	- [Worker and asset semantics](#worker-and-asset-semantics)
8	- [Routes zones and domains](#routes-zones-and-domains)
9	- [Bindings and storage](#bindings-and-storage)
10	- [Website origin rules](#website-origin-rules)
11	- [Secrets](#secrets)
12	- [Observability](#observability)
13	- [State](#state)
14	- [Readback checklist](#readback-checklist)
15	
16	## Ownership decisions
17	
18	Declare which system owns each Cloudflare lifecycle:
19	
20	- Worker or static-asset deployment;
21	- routes and custom domains;
22	- DNS/zone configuration;
23	- R2, D1, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, or Secrets Store;
24	- environment secrets and bindings;
25	- logs, metrics, traces, and observability destinations;
26	- remote state infrastructure.
27	
28	Do not assume Alchemy owns all Cloudflare resources because it owns one Worker.
29	
30	## File ownership
31	
32	For a small graph:
33	
34	```text
35	src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts
36	```
37	
38	For a substantial graph:
39	
40	```text
41	src/lib/build/cloudflare/
42	  stack.ts
43	  website.ts
44	  worker.ts
45	  storage.ts
46	  routes.ts
47	  secrets.ts
48	  observability.ts
49	```
50	
51	Keep stage/config Schemas outside provider declarations when other providers share them.
52	
53	## Worker and asset semantics
54	
55	Make asset routing policy explicit. In particular, distinguish asset-first and Worker-first behaviour and test the intended choice. A deployed Worker and green CI do not prove that static assets return the correct content type or bypass the Worker.
56	
57	Test:
58	
59	- root document;
60	- hashed CSS and JavaScript assets;
61	- missing assets;
62	- API paths;
63	- redirects;
64	- cache headers;
65	- content types;
66	- route precedence.
67	
68	Record compatibility date, compatibility flags, runtime limits, module format, and bundler inputs in a stable typed owner. Keep application and deployment configuration aligned through one contract or an invariant test.
69	
70	## Routes, zones, and domains
71	
72	Treat a zone or domain as foreign unless this repository creates and owns it.
73	
74	- Read the target zone before applying routes.
75	- Adopt only under explicit authority.
76	- Default adopted zones and routes to retain.
77	- Restrict Production route adoption to the Production stage.
78	- Reject a route whose account/zone does not match the authority record.
79	- Read back the route pattern and bound Worker after apply.
80	- Prove the public host independently.
81	
82	Do not infer route correctness from a Worker URL.
83	
84	## Bindings and storage
85	
86	Model each binding as typed desired state:
87	
88	- binding name;
89	- resource kind;
90	- physical resource identity;
91	- stage/environment;
92	- creation/adoption policy;
93	- removal policy.
94	
95	Assert that application code and deployment configuration use the same binding names. For Durable Objects, include class name, migration/tag policy, and deployment sequencing. For R2/D1/KV, make data retention explicit and default destructive deletion to forbidden until authorised.
96	
97	## Website origin rules
98	
99	An origin is the protocol and host, with an optional port, such as
100	`http://127.0.0.1:3210`. The deployed host owns that address. Applications must
101	never hard-code it or build it from a stage, Worker name, account subdomain,
102	custom domain or development port.
103	
104	For Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81`, use the native self URL binding on the host that
105	needs its own address:
106	
107	```typescript
108	const website =
109	  yield *
110	  Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Website", {
111	    rootDir: "apps/web",
112	    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
113	  });
114	
115	// The same binding works in a native Worker declaration.
116	const api =
117	  yield *
118	  Cloudflare.Worker("Api", {
119	    main: "./src/worker.ts",
120	    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
121	  });
122	```
123	
124	Alchemy resolves this binding to the local development proxy during local
125	development, the deployed `workers.dev` address, or the configured custom
126	domain. Do not add separate local/cloud address formulas or a copied-address
127	fallback. For Vite browser code, a `VITE_`-prefixed self URL binding uses the
128	same native resolution before the client bundle is built.
129	
130	It is valid to declare a chosen custom domain as infrastructure input, for
131	example `domain: "app.example.com"`. Keep the application's own
132	`PUBLIC_ORIGIN` bound to `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`; do not repeat that domain in
133	its environment or build `"https://" + domain` there. Aliases and incoming
134	request origins are separate from the host's configured canonical address.
135	
136	The native Effect Worker host supplies a ConfigProvider from its resolved
137	bindings. Application Layers consume the address with
138	`yield* Config.schema(OwnedOrigin, "PUBLIC_ORIGIN")` during runtime startup.
139	Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure route Layers, or read it while constructing an
140	existing service with `Layer.effect`. Reuse the host provider, owning Schema
141	and [general configuration pattern](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
142	instead of adding an address-only Context service. For a Website whose framework
143	does not supply that provider, use its existing narrow host adapter to check
144	owned bindings and pass only public settings to the browser.
145	
146	Beta.79 also supports `yield* Cloudflare.Worker.URL` in native Worker
147	initialisation. That yield attaches the binding and returns a deferred Effect,
148	not the address string. Running the returned Effect requires the native
149	`RuntimeContext`, where the binding is populated. Check the phase and lifetime
150	before using this accessor; the explicit env binding plus checked Config is the
151	startup path above. Do not read runtime bindings during graph planning or add a
152	new runtime to obtain them.
153	
154	For a different host, use that resource's native Output, such as `api.url`.
155	Pass the Output to the receiving resource; check its resolved value with the
156	owning Schema when application code reads the binding. If the native address
157	can be absent, preserve that absence as `null` for an env binding and reject it
158	with the Schema. Do not replace an absent Output with a guessed address.
159	
160	Keep expected validation failures typed. Beta.79's `Output.mapEffect` callback
161	accepts no expected errors, so do not force Schema decoding into it with
162	`Effect.orDie`. `Output.map` may select a checked resource attribute or represent
163	absence; it must not reconstruct the hostname. Resolve and decode Outputs
164	separately before writing workflow or receipt values.
165	
166	Check the selected Alchemy version's self URL, Vite, native Worker and local
167	provider APIs before copying this example. See the
168	[matching primary sources](../sources.md#cloudflare-website-origins).
169	Local source/type checks do not prove live domain routing.
170	
171	## Separate Website and native API Workers
172	
173	Use standard Website.Vite for the frontend and a native Effect Worker for the
174	API. The root stack deploys both with exact same-stage service/public bindings.
175	Preview has its own API; a Website preview parent does not authorise using the
176	Production API. Do not wrap TanStack in a backend Worker or recreate an API
177	runtime around the native incoming request fibre.
178	
179	Check the installed Alchemy build/runtime mechanism before reading deployment
180	services in a Worker declaration. The qualified beta.81 runtime build guard
181	removes stack-only requirements from the uploaded entry. Test the real native
182	entry without those services, return from startup, then request and release
183	resources. A typecheck or successful upload alone does not prove startup.
184	
185	Test browser CORS with the native client's actual headers and an actual browser
186	call. Tracing headers b3 and traceparent are part of the qualified client's
187	request; disabling tracing to avoid preflight is not a correction. Separate
188	remote MCP Origin validation from matching-origin Website WebMCP registration.
189	
190	## Preview environments without provider patches
191	
192	Check the installed ordinary Worker and Worker Preview providers separately.
193	A declared observability type or an existing Preview retaining earlier settings
194	does not prove that a newly created Preview receives those settings. Check both
195	create and update paths and read back a new deployment.
196	
197	When required Preview settings lack native support, consider an ordinary
198	stage-owned Website Worker alongside its stage-owned API before patching the
199	provider. Keep exact stage names, self URL bindings and native log/trace
200	destinations. This changes the Preview URL and teardown owner; confirm that
201	tradeoff. For a mode change, use a distinct native resource identity, such as
202	`Namespace.push`, and inspect the create/delete plan so the former parent cannot
203	be overwritten. Preserve production identities and shared state.
204	
205	Ordinary workers.dev Websites need their own indexing policy. Cloudflare's
206	[`_headers` file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/)
207	covers static assets; it does not cover Worker-generated replies. Apply the
208	checked stage policy through the existing framework response adapter, test
209	pages, errors, machine replies and assets, and keep production indexable.
210	Update CI addresses, Preview comments and trace queries for distinct Worker
211	names while preserving historical Preview records.
212	
213	## Secrets
214	
215	Prefer provider-managed secret references or Secrets Store bindings over plaintext workflow values.
216	
217	- Acquire credentials through redacted Config.
218	- Validate secret binding names and stage.
219	- Never emit values in plans, logs, outputs, or receipts.
220	- Separate credential issuance from resource apply.
221	- Read back metadata or binding presence, never the secret.
222	- Revoke disposable credentials after lifecycle proof.
223	
224	Removing a secret declaration may leave the old binding on the deployed Worker.
225	Check the active version's binding names and types; a no-change plan does not
226	prove removal. Prefer a supported native Alchemy deletion operation. If the
227	installed provider has none, record the residue and request an exact one-off
228	ownership exception before a provider write. Do not introduce a dependency
229	patch, custom resource or placeholder secret to conceal the gap. Keep shared
230	token revocation separate from binding removal. See the
231	[hosted telemetry cutover](../effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).
232	
233	## Observability
234	
235	Cloudflare platform observability and application telemetry are separate sources.
236	
237	For Cloudflare-native logs or destinations:
238	
239	- identify Worker/service/environment/stage;
240	- define retention and sampling;
241	- read back the destination/binding;
242	- query the downstream provider.
243	
244	For Effect OTLP export:
245	
246	- keep endpoint/token in a redacted binding;
247	- decode the binding at application ingress;
248	- attach one exporter Layer to the runtime;
249	- preserve `waitUntil` or the host completion mechanism;
250	- test transport wiring;
251	- query Axiom independently before claiming ingestion.
252	
253	## State
254	
255	If Cloudflare backs Alchemy state, document bootstrap and recovery. Do not create a circular dependency between the state backend and the graph it stores. Use a separate bootstrap stack or a tested provider-supported mechanism where necessary.
256	
257	Start with the installed native `Cloudflare.state()` setup and maintenance
258	behaviour. In the qualified beta.80 source, `--yes` permits automatic creation
259	and upgrades; pending setup can also be recovered. An existing-only rule is a
260	separate project choice. Check it before building a custom state client. Native
261	Website `domain.redirects` likewise has shared-list and failure semantics that
262	must be understood before promising stronger preservation. See
263	[native migrations](../operations/native-migrations.md#start-with-the-standard-behaviour)
264	and its pinned sources.
265	
266	## Readback checklist
267	
268	After apply, query the Cloudflare API for:
269	
270	- account and zone identity;
271	- Worker/script/service name;
272	- deployment/version identifier where available;
273	- routes/domains;
274	- bindings and safe resource IDs;
275	- compatibility settings;
276	- observability configuration;
277	- storage resource presence.
278	
279	Then run the public route/asset journey. Report any unavailable readback as a non-claim.
280	
281	### Website loader transport
282	
283	Choose native Effect HTTP GET endpoints for public reads needing CDN caching.
284	SSR uses native `HttpApiClient.make` with Alchemy's public
285	`fromCloudflareFetcher`/`toHttpClient` private same-stage binding transport;
286	browser loaders call the checked public API directly with FetchHttpClient.
287	Native `AtomHttpApi.Service` shares `browserRuntime.factory` and the existing
288	router/React registry. Use native query atoms for component-owned reactive
289	reads; loader-only reads call the generated client and let TanStack own their
290	freshness. Local `createIsomorphicFn` branches create no endpoint.
291	
292	Do not add Website server-function wrappers, proxy routes, loader atoms,
293	replica domain client services or custom response codecs merely for these reads.
294	Use native RPC deliberately when its procedure/streaming model fits the feature;
295	its POST replies are a separate caching decision. The official
296	[full-stack example](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/full-stack-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/)
297	uses a Website proxy and AtomRpc.Service as example choices. Native Service
298	factories can share one registry; inspect installed APIs rather than rejecting
299	them because an existing Atom runtime is present.
300	
301	Follow [React ownership](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md#native-public-http-reads-for-a-separate-website-and-api)
302	for native request deadlines, cancellation, plain successful loader data and
303	single error translation. Verify private SSR, actual browser headers/CORS,
304	complete first HTML and stage pairing separately.
305	
306	### Native public response caching
307	
308	First inspect the matching Alchemy repo, installed types and official
309	[Workers Cache guide](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/cache/). In the
310	qualified beta.81, use `yield* Cloudflare.cache({ crossVersionCache: false })`
311	in native Worker construction **before** a plan-only return, and
312	`cache: { enabled: true, crossVersionCache: false }` on `Website.Vite`.
313	These declare native version-scoped storage. They do not choose which application
314	responses are public or their freshness. Do not build an owned Cache API runtime,
315	cache-key framework, purge service or Alchemy provider patch.
316	
317	Enable the portable [native Cloudflare cache rule](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
318	in the owned Cloudflare application paths to prevent a second global Cache API
319	runtime. Prove native declarations and backend Effect caches still pass. The
320	rule checks code ownership; hosted requests must separately prove reuse.
321	
322	Choose response policy explicitly. For example, Common Practice uses seven-day
323	CDN freshness with browser `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` and
324	`Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-if-error=0`.
325	Seven days is that project's product decision; qualify the target's own duration.
326	Cloudflare owns [CDN header precedence](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cdn-cache-control/);
327	Alchemy's local Cache API shim is a different path and does not prove that edge
328	behaviour. Preserve the headers and qualify actual hosted reuse separately.
329	TanStack loader freshness is another choice (the starter uses one minute),
330	separate from browser HTTP reuse and native Worker cache freshness. Freshness
331	allows reuse; it does not guarantee retention for seven days or a HIT on every
332	request. Eviction, regions, new versions, request variants and private responses
333	can cause misses. Cache hits may skip Worker execution and its request analytics.
334	
335	Cache only eligible public GET/HEAD responses. Preserve stricter Cache-Control,
336	CDN-Cache-Control and Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control instructions; private/no-store,
337	failures and Set-Cookie responses remain uncacheable. Preserve native status,
338	headers, cookies, body/stream and cancellation when adapting responses. Use a
339	small app-owned eligibility/header decision when needed; do not create an
340	independent caching library or parse durations that native storage already owns.
341	
342	GET selection fields belong in the path/query, not a request body. Native clients
343	encode endpoint query fields and the URL distinguishes `format=data`, Markdown,
344	HTML and images. `Vary` supplies additional response variants: preserve API CORS
345	`Vary: Origin` and negotiated page `Vary: Accept`.
346	
347	Every response that can be served at one URL must carry the same `Vary` set.
348	That includes the page HTML, its Accept-negotiated Markdown redirect and any
349	400/406 negotiation reply. When one variant names fewer request headers than
350	another, the stored variants disagree and each evicts the other: the page and
351	its redirect then miss on every alternation. Discovery files and machine
352	siblings at their own URLs keep their own set.
353	
354	A matching `Vary` set is not enough on its own. A `no-store` reply at a page URL
355	can drop the stored page even when its `Vary` set is identical. Site saw a 406
356	for an unusual `Accept` header do this, and adad saw a `no-store` 308 do it.
357	Anyone could then empty a page's cache entry with one odd request. Give answers
358	that depend only on the request headers in the `Vary` set, such as negotiation
359	400/406 replies and permanent host or path redirects, the page's public cache
360	policy so they are stored as their own variants beside the page. Keep genuine
361	failures, such as an unavailable 503, uncached. A request carrying
362	`Authorization` does not evict: a hit is served before the Worker runs, because
363	Authorization is not in the key. So never rely on that header to keep
364	user-specific HTML off a public URL.
365	
366	Do not vary public HTML on `Cookie`. With `Vary: Cookie` the whole Cookie header
367	joins the cache key, so any unrelated cookie (bot management, analytics or
368	another subdomain's cookie) gives each visitor a private copy. Serve one public
369	HTML response per URL with the device default and apply a saved theme or
370	appearance before first paint with TanStack's `ScriptOnce`; see
371	[theme before first paint](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md#theme-and-appearance-before-first-paint).
372	The server then never reads the appearance cookie for cached HTML, so no
373	malformed-cookie private path is needed. Never assume a Cookie variant makes
374	user-specific content public.
375	
376	With cross-version sharing disabled, a new Worker version starts a separate
377	cache. Include authored content in both API and Website native build/memo inputs,
378	and deploy them together so a content-only change refreshes JSON and HTML.
379	The stack coordinates deployment but activation is not atomic. Version-scoped
380	storage is not strict at the moment of a switch: adad saw a reply from the
381	outgoing version stay stored and be served for over a minute to the new version
382	until a further version replaced it. Check replies after every switch, and
383	especially after a change that alters a path's status, redirects or `Vary`. Prove this with a
384	controlled Preview content change, both new version IDs and changed JSON/HTML;
385	restore the fixture before Production. Do not claim deployment invalidation from
386	a successful plan or one Worker's new version alone.
387	
388	Hosted qualification consumes the first response and repeats the exact ordinary
389	URL/headers to observe `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` and Age. A first request after a
390	version change may be MISS. Inspect request `Cache-Control`/browser reload headers
391	and repeat them rather than assuming `no-cache` always bypasses native storage.
392	Do not add cache-busting queries or sleeps to force a passing test. Warm format,
393	Accept and Origin variants in both orders. At one page URL, warm the HTML, then
394	its negotiated Markdown redirect, then the HTML again (and the reverse order);
395	every repeat must stay a HIT. Send a saved-appearance cookie and an unrelated
396	cookie and confirm both receive the shared HTML. At a warmed page URL, send a
397	request that yields a negotiation 400/406, then the ordinary page again: it must
398	stay a HIT, and repeating the 400/406 request must HIT too. Verify private and error
399	responses remain uncached and HEAD follows native semantics. Read back cache
400	options on both Workers and their current versions. A local image/render cache,
401	HTTP headers alone, or an internal service-binding call is not public edge-cache
402	proof. Keep local, deployment, provider, public URL and browser evidence separate.

1	---
2	name: alchemy-iac
3	description: Design, implement, audit, or migrate governed Alchemy infrastructure-as-code in Effect TypeScript repositories. Use for alchemy.run.ts entrypoints, provider Layers, Cloudflare resources, Axiom datasets or dashboards, WorkOS redirect configuration, Vercel project integration, custom Alchemy Resources or Actions, stage and state design, infrastructure file conventions, deployment authority, provider readback, receipts, drift, teardown, and infrastructure tests. Also use when deciding that Alchemy should not own a hosted resource.
4	---
5	
6	# Alchemy IaC
7	
8	Build infrastructure as an explicit, typed, reviewable resource graph. Keep mutation authority, provider ownership, state, stage identity, provider readback, and public behaviour as separate claims.
9	
10	Use this skill with `$strict-effect-ts` whenever infrastructure code contains material Effect programs. Also load repository-local `AGENTS.md`, `$repo-structure`, `$package-structure`, and provider-specific instructions when available.
11	
12	## Non-negotiable rules
13	
14	1. Inspect the exact checkout, instructions, installed Alchemy version, existing entrypoints, active infrastructure packages, workflows, and dirty state before proposing a structure.
15	2. Establish who owns each resource before writing code. Do not add Alchemy merely because a provider exists.
16	3. Treat a tool capability as different from authority. Require an explicit operation, resource scope, stage, credential source, and mutation boundary.
17	4. Keep `alchemy.run.ts` a composition root. Decode inputs, select providers and state, compose named stacks, and return typed outputs. Move domain policy into stable owner modules.
18	5. Decode all external input at ingress with Effect Schema or Config. Keep secrets redacted. Never let `unknown`, raw JSON, primitive environment strings, or provider SDK objects cross the boundary.
19	6. Model provider dependencies as Layers. Construct them once at the application root. Do not import or expose raw provider clients from domain services.
20	7. Separate desired-state planning from mutation. A plan classifies change; it does not authorise apply.
21	8. Make custom resource reconciliation convergent and deletion explicit. Default adopted or foreign resources to `retain`.
22	9. Resolve Alchemy Outputs before persisting durable receipts or crossing process boundaries.
23	10. Prove source identity, provider identity, Preview, Production, and public behaviour independently. A green workflow, Alchemy state, successful exporter response, or HTTP 200 is not interchangeable with provider or journey proof.
24	11. Make every stage collision-resistant. Include stable logical names and explicit physical identity where provider defaults are ambiguous.
25	12. Prefer no IaC over ceremonial IaC. If Vercel Git, a provider console, or another declared owner already governs the lifecycle, document the boundary and omit the resource graph unless Alchemy has a narrow named role.
26	13. Never write credentials, bearer tokens, state secrets, raw provider payloads, local absolute paths, or unbounded logs into receipts.
27	14. Do not mutate providers, issue credentials, deploy, destroy, push, or publish merely because this skill is loaded. Follow the user's exact authority.
28	15. Never cross an `apps/**` or `packages/**` workspace boundary through a relative filesystem import. Use an explicit package or app export. If substantial multi-provider infrastructure needs an app-owned contract, move the shared contract and its real owner into an infrastructure package instead of exporting an app-internal path.
29	16. Never hard-code or construct an application's own deployed website address. For Cloudflare Website.Vite and native Worker hosts, bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` on that host's `env`. Use native resource Outputs for another host's address and keep Schema validation when either value enters application code. Read fixed runtime settings through the host's ConfigProvider in their owning Layers. A chosen custom domain belongs in infrastructure input; do not copy it into application origin configuration. See the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](references/providers/cloudflare.md).
30	17. For Doppler-backed stacks, declare native sources once: Doppler, optional ignored `.env`, then `Secrets.ProcessEnv({ disabled: true })`. `.env` wins in local and hosted runs. Native sign-in uses a config-scoped read-only runner token or native profile. Follow [native sources and sign-in](references/effect/services-config-and-errors.md#native-doppler-and-dotenv-sources); remove superseded CLI injection and competing current instructions during the cutover.
31	
32	## Workflow
33	
34	### 1. Discover the current contract
35	
36	Read, in order:
37	
38	1. Repository and package instructions.
39	2. Current architecture and deployment documentation.
40	3. `package.json`, lockfile, and installed Alchemy/Effect/provider versions.
41	4. `alchemy*.run.ts`, infrastructure packages, provider modules, workflows, tests, and receipts.
42	5. Workspace manifests and export maps, plus a source scan for relative imports that reach into `apps/**` or `packages/**`.
43	6. Provider ownership and live-readback instructions.
44	7. Git status for every checkout that may be edited.
45	
46	Record the current owner of each resource and each claim. Do not use a stale SPEC, historical receipt, or another worktree as current truth.
47	
48	Before adding custom guards, separate confirmed requirements from inherited
49	project restrictions and check ordinary native behaviour. When removing patches
50	or custom providers, read [native migrations](references/operations/native-migrations.md)
51	for retention, storage maintenance, saved-record conversion, provider retirement
52	and fresh-install proof. Check both matching Alchemy and Effect source; newer
53	upstream code does not select an upgrade.
54	
55	### 2. Decide whether Alchemy belongs
56	
57	For every proposed resource, answer:
58	
59	- What lifecycle does Alchemy own: create, adopt, observe, configure, reconcile, or destroy?
60	- What system owns deployment provenance?
61	- Can the provider expose independent readback?
62	- Can the operation be retried safely?
63	- What happens on partial failure?
64	- What is the removal policy?
65	- Does the repository need this resource, or only documentation of another owner's boundary?
66	
67	Use [ownership and boundaries](references/architecture/ownership-and-boundaries.md) for the decision.
68	
69	### 3. Design identity before resources
70	
71	Define:
72	
73	- stack name;
74	- logical stage;
75	- environment;
76	- repository and application identity;
77	- branch/ref/revision where relevant;
78	- provider account, project, organisation, tenant, or zone;
79	- physical resource naming;
80	- state backend and state namespace;
81	- retention and teardown policy.
82	
83	Keep proof stages isolated from Preview and Production. See [stages, state, and identity](references/architecture/stages-state-and-identity.md).
84	
85	### 4. Choose a file layout
86	
87	Start small. Extract only stable semantic owners.
88	
89	A compact application normally uses:
90	
91	```text
92	alchemy.run.ts
93	src/lib/build/
94	  schemas.ts
95	  cloudflare.ts
96	datasets/
97	  definitions.ts
98	  index.ts
99	dashboards/
100	  definitions.ts
101	  index.ts
102	  <dashboard>.ts
103	tools/infrastructure/
104	  preflight.ts
105	  readback.ts
106	  receipt.ts
107	```
108	
109	A reusable or multi-provider package normally uses:
110	
111	```text
112	packages/infrastructure/src/
113	  schemas.ts
114	  errors.ts
115	  service.ts
116	  live.layer.ts
117	  memory.layer.ts
118	  providers.ts
119	  inventory.ts
120	  drift.ts
121	  receipt.ts
122	  stacks/
123	  cloudflare/
124	  axiom/
125	  workos/
126	  vercel/
127	alchemy.run.ts
128	alchemy.preview.run.ts
129	alchemy.production.run.ts
130	```
131	
132	When a package owns the graph, root entrypoints, apps, tools and sibling
133	packages consume only explicit exports. Move shared Schemas and contracts with
134	the graph when they no longer belong to one app. Do not move only the stack and
135	leave it importing app internals through `../apps/**`.
136	
137	Do not create every listed file. Create a file only when it owns a coherent contract. Read [layout and composition](references/architecture/layout-and-composition.md) and [worked layouts and patterns](references/examples/layouts-and-patterns.md).
138	
139	### 5. Build a pure desired-state graph
140	
141	- Decode stage, authority, and configuration first.
142	- Declare typed catalogues for datasets, dashboards, routes, redirects, projects, and bindings.
143	- Give every resource a stable logical name.
144	- Keep provider graph construction deterministic.
145	- Keep direct environment access and runtime execution at the root adapter.
146	- Return only the outputs downstream consumers need.
147	- Do not run provider mutation from module import side effects.
148	
149	Read [resource graphs and Outputs](references/architecture/resource-graphs-and-outputs.md).
150	
151	### 6. Add provider ownership deliberately
152	
153	Load only the relevant provider references:
154	
155	- [Cloudflare](references/providers/cloudflare.md)
156	- [Axiom](references/providers/axiom.md)
157	- [PostHog projects, dashboards and capture bindings](references/providers/posthog.md)
158	- [WorkOS](references/providers/workos.md)
159	- [Vercel](references/providers/vercel.md)
160	- [custom Resources and Actions](references/providers/custom-resources.md)
161	
162	For multi-provider changes, write an ownership table before code:
163	
164	| Resource | Desired-state owner | Deployment owner | Readback source            | Removal policy |
165	| -------- | ------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------------- |
166	| Example  | Alchemy             | provider API     | independent provider query | retain/delete  |
167	
168	Treat “not managed by Alchemy” as a valid, reviewable answer.
169	
170	### 7. Gate plan and apply
171	
172	Before mutation:
173	
174	1. Resolve the exact stage and source revision.
175	2. Validate credential provenance and minimum capability.
176	3. Run capacity, entitlement, quota, and identity preflights.
177	4. Generate a plan.
178	5. Reject unexpected create, replace, delete, adoption, or cross-stage change.
179	6. Require the operation-specific authority.
180	7. Apply serially when provider ordering, rate limits, or uncertain writes demand it.
181	8. Read back through the provider independently.
182	9. Run the claim-matched public or application journey.
183	10. Emit a sanitised receipt.
184	
185	Read [authority, plan, and apply](references/operations/authority-plan-apply.md) and [readback, receipts, and claims](references/operations/readback-receipts-and-claims.md).
186	
187	### 8. Design recovery before Production
188	
189	Define retry, rollback, adoption, drift, partial-write recovery, and destroy semantics before enabling Production. Test retained-resource isolation and prove that a disposable stage can be destroyed without touching Preview or Production. Read [adoption, drift, recovery, and destroy](references/operations/adoption-drift-recovery-and-destroy.md).
190	
191	### 9. Verify proportionately
192	
193	Run the layers of proof relevant to the claim:
194	
195	1. static structure and policy;
196	2. typecheck and unit tests;
197	3. provider-free memory graph tests;
198	4. plan classification;
199	5. isolated provider apply;
200	6. provider readback;
201	7. application journey;
202	8. teardown and residue readback.
203	
204	Use [the verification matrix](references/testing/verification-matrix.md). State every skipped layer as a non-claim.
205	
206	### 10. Review documentation ownership
207	
208	Update the current architecture owner, runbook, and receipt contract when behaviour changes. Do not copy live identities into generic documentation. Do not turn a historical receipt into a mutable design document.
209	
210	## Alchemy with Effect
211	
212	Use Effect for configuration, provider adapters, custom providers, plans, readback, retry, timeouts, concurrency, structured errors, receipts, logging, tracing, and tests. Keep Alchemy's root runtime boundary thin.
213	
214	Read:
215	
216	- [Effect services, Config, Schema, and errors](references/effect/services-config-and-errors.md)
217	- [infrastructure observability](references/effect/observability.md)
218	- [hosted web telemetry](references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md) for the
219	  separate Website/API execution, Cloudflare traces, Axiom logs and metrics,
220	  event finalisation and correctly named timing measures
221	- `$strict-effect-ts` for the full language policy
222	
223	## Review checklist
224	
225	Reject the change if any answer is unclear:
226	
227	- Is the resource lifecycle owner explicit?
228	- Is the current stage decoded rather than inferred from a loose string?
229	- Are physical names collision-resistant?
230	- Is state ownership explicit?
231	- Are adopted resources retained by default?
232	- Are provider Layers composed at the root?
233	- Are SDK/HTTP outputs decoded immediately?
234	- Are plan and apply separately authorised?
235	- Are replacement and deletion classified?
236	- Is provider readback independent of state?
237	- Is public behaviour proved separately?
238	- Are receipts portable, bounded, and secret-negative?
239	- Can a proof stage be destroyed without affecting Production?
240	- Is the file layout semantic rather than ceremonial?
241	- Does every cross-app or cross-package import use an explicit workspace export?
242	- Does each host receive its own origin from the native self URL binding, and other hosts' addresses from native Outputs, with Schema checks in application code?
243	- Does the repository actually need Alchemy for this lifecycle?
244	- Does each remaining custom guard answer a current requirement that native behaviour cannot satisfy?
245	- If patches are removed, can the candidate read existing saved records, retire old provider registrations in order and recover after conversion?
246	- For patch removal, has the same unpatched release been qualified from every importing owner in a fresh installation and real bundle?
247	
248	Consult [anti-patterns](references/examples/anti-patterns.md) during review.
249	
250	## Reference map
251	
252	Architecture:
253	
254	- [ownership and boundaries](references/architecture/ownership-and-boundaries.md)
255	- [layout and composition](references/architecture/layout-and-composition.md)
256	- [stages, state, and identity](references/architecture/stages-state-and-identity.md)
257	- [resource graphs and Outputs](references/architecture/resource-graphs-and-outputs.md)
258	
259	Providers:
260	
261	- [Cloudflare](references/providers/cloudflare.md)
262	- [Axiom](references/providers/axiom.md)
263	- [PostHog projects, dashboards and capture bindings](references/providers/posthog.md)
264	- [WorkOS](references/providers/workos.md)
265	- [Vercel](references/providers/vercel.md)
266	- [custom Resources and Actions](references/providers/custom-resources.md)
267	
268	Operations:
269	
270	- [authority, plan, and apply](references/operations/authority-plan-apply.md)
271	- [readback, receipts, and claims](references/operations/readback-receipts-and-claims.md)
272	- [adoption, drift, recovery, and destroy](references/operations/adoption-drift-recovery-and-destroy.md)
273	- [native migrations and unpatched-package policy](references/operations/native-migrations.md)
274	
275	Effect and testing:
276	
277	- [services, Config, Schema, and errors](references/effect/services-config-and-errors.md)
278	- [observability](references/effect/observability.md)
279	- [hosted web telemetry](references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md)
280	- [PostHog application, backend capture and native HTTP relay](references/effect/posthog-analytics.md)
281	- [verification matrix](references/testing/verification-matrix.md)
282	
283	Examples and provenance:
284	
285	- [layouts and patterns](references/examples/layouts-and-patterns.md)
286	- [anti-patterns](references/examples/anti-patterns.md)
287	- [primary sources and version policy](references/sources.md)
288	
289	## Immutable checked infrastructure
290	
291	Infrastructure also uses one Schema owner and immutable Effect collections.
292	Infer contract types, reuse branded fields and whole-record checks, decode real
293	inputs/provider replies once and trust checked internal values. New constrained
294	values use checked constructors with named errors. Use Option for absence and
295	exhaustive Match for closed plan/resource alternatives; use folds/traversals
296	instead of loops or local mutation. Readonly structured cache keys require the
297	installed equality/hash and cleanup proof. Keep historical state/receipt formats
298	and hashes compatible when changing a codec. Research the cloned v4 source and
299	reconcile it with the receiving installation; copying a qualified snapshot does
300	not choose its dependency versions, resources, identities or credentials.
301	
302	## Prefer existing native request and cache owners
303	
304	Before adding a request wrapper, client service, loader Atom or cache, inspect
305	matching installed APIs and current upstream examples. For public cached reads,
306	follow the existing native HTTP/Atom/TanStack and Cloudflare cache owners; remove
307	pass-through code that duplicates their loading, decoding, lifecycle or storage.
308	Keep real feature policy, checked host adapters and one application runner.

content.content:
Review a native Alchemy plan for the exact stage and revision. Expected changes:

- Create logical `Backend` as `common-practice-<stage>-backend` on a new stage's
  first apply. Existing stages update that same owner. Production keeps
  `api.withcommonpractice.com` and its retained legacy API alias, with workers.dev
  off. Non-production APIs expose their own workers.dev addresses.
- Update the existing Website with its same-stage `BACKEND`, checked
  `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL` and native self address `COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`. Preserve the Website's
  production name and apex domain, cache and compatibility settings. Preview
  stages own a distinct Website Worker; the first migration replaces only their
  former Worker Preview as described above.
- Production Website uses `workersDev: false`; its custom domains remain live.
  Other Website stages keep their stable workers.dev address with
  `previewsEnabled: false`. PR Workers are independent of production, so no
  extra production version URL is needed. Inspect native drift output as well
  as its exit status: native drift can exit successfully while reporting changes.
- Preserve explicit hosted log and trace destination settings. Keep renderer, WASM and authored
  Markdown in the API bundle and out of the browser bundle. Shared telemetry
  stacks/resources keep their existing identities and are not redeployed by
  this split.

Inspect the explicitly approved Preview migration above; investigate any other
Website replacement, adoption/deletion, cross-stage
bindings, or changes to shared zone settings, DNSSEC, crawler policy and telemetry
resources before applying. Native API domain reconciliation is the authorised
hostname change; do not create DNS by hand. User authority for this delivery
includes PR publication, Preview, merge and production apply. Future changes
still need their own scope. Use only native Alchemy commands.

After apply, independently read both Workers' active versions, Website binding
names/targets, API public addresses and domain ownership. Never print binding
secret values. Run read-only hosted checks against both checked output addresses:

```sh
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_WEBSITE_URL=https://withcommonpractice.com \
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_API_URL=https://api.withcommonpractice.com bun run test:public
```

Preview uses its own output addresses, for example Website
`https://common-practice-pr-42.coopercorbett.workers.dev` and API
`https://common-practice-pr-42-backend.coopercorbett.workers.dev`. These are separate Workers;
Preview must never advertise or bind production's API.

The public suite checks HTML, canonical metadata, Markdown/PNG, all requested
Content formats through native HttpApiClient, named missing-page errors, discovery/digest
addresses, latest MCP discover/list/call with and without a third-party browser
Origin, valid preflight and malformed-Origin rejection. Website legacy
`/api/*`, `/rpc` and `/mcp` must return 404 without redirects. The API's retired
`/rpc` endpoint must also return uncached 404 for GET and POST, with no
compatibility handler. Successful representations remain public; failures remain uncached. Public MCP is anonymous
and supports the published `2026-07-28` protocol; it is available at API `/mcp`.

Also check actual browser navigation/refresh and exact-origin WebMCP registration.
The read-only isitagentready scan may supplement this evidence; it cannot prove
that an ordinary or third-party agent can connect/list/call. Hosted cancellation,
exporter timing, Axiom ingestion and cross-Worker span parents are separate
checks. Neither a response-ready log nor HTTP 200 proves stream completion or
later log delivery. Local tests do prove deterministic cancellation/finalisers.

Record source revision, stage, Worker identities, addresses, CI, apply result,
provider readback, browser and public checks in dated evidence. A final native
plan should report no changes; production drift must be read for reported drift,
because its successful exit is not a no-drift assertion. Never use `--repair`
as a substitute for an authorised plan/apply. Recovery deploys a known-good
revision through native Alchemy; do not bypass the owner with provider writes.

## Telemetry checks
independent `common-practice-<stage>-backend` services.

The approved Worker-name replacement was limited to the two stateless production
services. Its one-time patch exposed an explicit name change before deferred
bindings resolved and used delete-first for same-account name replacements.
The one-time apply temporarily disabled retention so the old services released
their domains. Normal production retention was restored immediately afterwards.
Never reuse that exception for a service with stored data without its own review.
The rename is complete and that patch is removed. Keep current physical names
stable; a later rename needs its own native plan and domain-handover review.

The purchased zone has separate retained `CommonPractice*` declarations. Native
Alchemy preserves path and query on redirects from new `www`, old apex and old
`www`. The old API is a serving alias, without redirects, for the current
HTTP and native MCP endpoints. The removed publishing RPC endpoint is not
retained on either API hostname. Let native Alchemy resolve each hostname's own zone. Both
registrations stay active during the transition.

Cloudflare token labels were renamed in place; their values, expiry and grants
were preserved. Only production gained the same five zone permissions for the
verified new zone. Both Axiom key replacements are complete; their grants and expiry were preserved.
The current ingestion key is `common-practice-telemetry-ingest`; management is
`common-practice-alchemy-management-20260923`. Their old IDs were revoked after
fresh storage checks. That one-off approval to use Site's admin key does not
extend to later rotations.

PostHog captures `common_practice_*` events and queries both generations. Its
existing projects and stored data stay in place. New Axiom logs and custom trace
fields use `common-practice` / `common-practice.*`. Following the platform-delivery
cutover, request-log readers accept only the new console-record format and metric
charts are removed. Historical trace support remains. Shared Site datasets and
historical metric records remain Site-owned.

The 3 October record renames used native `renamedFrom` declarations. Their
former Axiom aliases were removed after the 4 October hard cutover; the legacy
Cloudflare zone aliases remain historical rename inputs. Keep token props
unchanged to avoid another rotation. The five replacement dashboards now have
Common Practice link IDs. Axiom rejects changing an existing UID in place, so
this cutover created new objects and deleted the five old objects instead.

The new skill is the only advertised address. The old skill URL returns 308 to
the new skill on the same-stage API. Keep the old domain registered: website
links redirect, and the old API serves HTTP/MCP clients while advertising
the new primary API. Do not turn POST API aliases into website-style 301 redirects.

After a release, check both services, redirects with path/query, old API GET and
MCP POSTs and retired `/rpc` 404s, discovery documents, generated images, browser layout and WebMCP,
provider settings and trace consumers. Replan each affected stack. Recovery must
review the native plans and current physical names; blindly reverting to old
Worker names causes another replacement and domain handover.

## Original custom-domain rollout

The production stack declares the `departmentofagenticwork.com` zone, its settings,
DNSSEC, a bot policy and the Website's custom domain (see the
[SPEC](../exec-plans/custom-domain.md) and ARCHITECTURE.md). Roll it out in the
SPEC's three production changes, each with its own reviewed plan and evidence.

**Token permissions.** The original rollout required the owner to add Common Practice-zone
permissions to the `common-practice/prd` token: Zone Settings Edit, DNS Edit, Bot Management
Edit, and the permissions for Worker custom domains and redirect rules. The
dated custom-domain evidence records that approved rollout. Read current
provider state before claiming a later plan can use those permissions. Preserve
the token's other permissions and expiry; keep zone permissions scoped to
`departmentofagenticwork.com`. This runbook does not authorise changing a token.

**Step 1 plan.** A production plan with the declarations reports, and the review
rejects anything else: 7 to create (`DawTls13`, `DawMinimumTlsVersion`,
`DawBrowserIntegrityCheck`, `DawSecurityLevel`, `DawAlwaysUseHttps`, `DawDnssec`,
`DawBotManagement`), 1 adopted (`DawZone`), and the Website update. Before the first
apply, read the zone's current settings and bot management read-only and record them.

**Checks after apply.** Apex 200; `www` 301 to the apex with path and query; a TLS 1.3
and a TLS 1.2 handshake succeed and TLS 1.1 is refused; DNSSEC signing, the parent DS
record present and a validating resolver answering (`pending` is not active); a
user-agent matrix (at least `Python-urllib`, `libwww-perl`, `python-requests`,
`curl`, `Wget`, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot and an empty agent) where
every agent gets 200; and the zone settings read back from Cloudflare equal the
declaration.

**Rollback.** Remove the `domain` block to detach the domain. The retained zone
settings only loosen the edge and stay.

**Step 2 (the origin).** The plan shows only the Website update, because the code
changed (Alchemy hashes the `apps/web` source tree, so any edit there, even to a test,
plans a new Worker version; a docs-only edit does not); no zone, setting, DNSSEC or bot resource may change. After apply: the apex
serves the new `Link` header, canonical links, sitemap and card; the served
`SKILL.md` hashed with `shasum -a 256` equals the digest in
`/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`; `POST https://isitagentready.com/api/scan`
with the apex reports level 4; and the production dashboards show traffic on the
apex (the trace filter accepted both origins until step 3). The trace dashboards are a
second stack: run `bun run axiom:plan`, review it (three dashboard updates) and apply
with `bun run axiom:deploy --yes`. Roll back by reverting the pull request and applying
both stacks again.

**Step 3 (`workers.dev` off, historical 30 September rollout).** Production set
`workersDev: { enabled: false, previewsEnabled: true }`; the plan is the Website
update, and `axiom:plan` shows the three trace dashboards. Before merging, open a
pull request with the change and confirm its Preview workflow deploys and its
Preview URL answers. That proves the change deploys only, because a Preview does not
write the production Worker's setting. After apply: the apex is still 200,
`https://common-practice-production.coopercorbett.workers.dev/` no longer serves, and a fresh pull
request's Preview deploys and answers (roll back at once if it does not). Apply
`axiom:deploy --yes` too, for the apex-only trace filter. Roll back by reverting the
pull request, which restores `workersDev`, the allowed origin and the old trace filter
together, and applying both stacks.

The current 6 October policy is `workersDev: false` on production and
`{ enabled: true, previewsEnabled: false }` on other Websites. Independent PR
Workers replace the parent Preview dependency above. Use native Alchemy for this
policy; no provider patch or direct settings write is required.

## PostHog project setup and deliberate Preview capture

`alchemy.posthog.run.ts` is the separate `common-practice-analytics` stack at stage
`production`. It manages two projects, **Common Practice production** and **Common Practice preview**,
with Website usage and API usage dashboards in each. Its first plan must show
only those two projects, four dashboards, twelve insights and twelve tiles.
It must not adopt or change the organisation's other projects. The approved
personal organisation is Cooper, ID `019bb70c-c87e-0000-47a6-c4fdc3043f42`.
Check the signed-in account and organisation before credential setup.

before any change, so the comparison is real. A Free-plan zone may reject some

field is recorded and dropped, not worked around.

### 5.3 The `workers.dev` address

Alchemy's `workersDev` has separate stable-address and version-preview switches.
Production now declares `workersDev: false`, so it serves only its custom domains.
PR Websites are independent `common-practice-pr-<number>` Workers; their stable
addresses remain enabled with `previewsEnabled: false`. Local and other hosted
Website stages use the same stable-address policy.

The 30 September rollout kept production version URLs because PRs then used its
native Worker Preview. That dependency ended with the 6 October stage-owned
Preview design. Unused version URLs also create a beta.79 readback difference:
upload saves the version address, while native Worker read returns domains and
stable addresses only. Remove the unused addresses through native policy;
do not patch provider readback or suppress drift. Deployment proof is separate
from this declaration.

### 5.4 The origin change

One origin becomes the new apex. The changes, each with its proof (section 8):

- `CanonicalUrl` accepts the new origin; `siteOrigin` is the new origin.

## 7. Authority and permissions

- Applying and even planning section 5 needs the Cloudflare token in `common-practice/prd`
  to gain permissions it does not have. Expected, to be confirmed by the T1
  read-only preflight and the provider's own errors: Zone Settings Edit, DNS
  Edit, Bot Management Edit, and whatever attaches a Worker custom domain and
  writes its redirect rule (a zone ruleset and Workers custom-domain permission).
  The site project's token needed DNS Edit and Zone Settings Edit for its
  equivalent work.
- Adding permissions is the owner's action and stays a separate decision, as in
  `docs/runbooks/deployment.md` (Secrets Store Edit). Preserve the token's other
  permissions and expiry. The permissions cover the whole zone; nothing else in it
  exists yet.
- Native Alchemy only plans and applies; no Wrangler or dashboard writes. The
  zone is adopted, never created or deleted, and retained on destroy.
- The `common-practice/stg_preview` credential and the Preview stages do not gain zone
  access.

or an Alchemy profile login; locally, pass the repository's existing Doppler
login for the one command without printing it:

```sh
DOPPLER_TOKEN="$(doppler configure get token --plain)" bun run production:plan
```

Do not copy Cloudflare values into the shell, a committed file or GitHub.

The Production token (`taxkit/prd`) is an account-owned token. On the
`taxkit.dev` zone it holds Zone DNS Settings Read, Zone Settings Write, DNS Write
(DNSSEC), Bot Management Write, Dynamic URL Redirects Write and Workers Routes
Write; on the account, Workers Scripts, Workers Observability and Secrets Store
Write. Change it with `cf accounts tokens update`, keeping its name, expiry and
existing policies, and record the change here. It expires on 18 November 2026.

## Preview

```sh
bun run pr:plan pr-<number>
bun run pr:deploy pr-<number>
bun run pr:destroy pr-<number>
```

`pr:deploy` builds the repository first. Preview uses its own API, never the
Production API. Destroy the stage when its pull request closes.

## Production

```sh
bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy
bun run production:drift
```

Review the plan. Production adopts and retains the `taxkit.dev` zone, DNS
settings, zone settings, DNSSEC and bot policy; a plan that would create, replace or delete the zone, or delete either
Worker, must stop. `production:drift` compares the deployed resources with
state.

## Check the deployment

1. Note both Worker version IDs from the deploy output.
2. Load the Website, a docs page and its `.md` page; calculate with and without
   JavaScript.
3. Check `https://www.taxkit.dev/<path>?<query>` returns a 301 to the same path
   and query on `taxkit.dev`.
4. Check API CORS from a browser page on another origin: public GETs and the
   calculation POST are allowed without credentials.
5. Repeat an eligible public GET with the same headers. The second response
   should show `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` and an `Age`. Calculation results,
   errors and `Set-Cookie` replies stay private and uncached.

## Rollback

Check out the previous working commit and run the same deploy command for the
stage. Cloudflare caches are version-scoped, so the redeployed versions start
with empty caches. Activation of the two Workers is not atomic; a short overlap
of old and new versions is possible.

## Known limits

- The native Alchemy redirect provider treats a failed read of the zone's
  shared redirect ruleset as an empty ruleset. A later successful write then
  holds only TaxKit's `www` rule and can remove redirect rules owned elsewhere
  in the zone. The `taxkit.dev` zone holds only TaxKit's own rule; check the
  zone's redirect rules before adding another owner. The Worker upload happens
  before the redirect rule is written.
- Seven-day Cloudflare freshness lets Cloudflare reuse a response; it does not
  guarantee that the cache keeps it.

| Resource | Owner | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TaxKitApi` | native Effect Worker from `api/worker` | Its own address from `Worker.URL`; `api.taxkit.dev` in Production. |
| `TaxKitWebsite` | `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` for `apps/web` | Its own address from `Worker.URL`; the API's address Output and the private `TAXKIT_API` binding. Production serves only `taxkit.dev`, with a native `www.taxkit.dev` redirect and no `workers.dev` address; other stages use their stable `workers.dev` address. No stage has version preview addresses. |
| `TaxKitProductionZone` | adopted and retained in `prod` only | Never created, replaced or deleted by the stack. |
| `TaxKitProductionDnsSettings` | retained in `prod` only | Matches the 7 October readback; registrar and records are not managed. |
| `TaxKitProduction*` zone settings | retained native `Cloudflare.Zone.Setting` in `prod` only | TLS 1.3 on with a TLS 1.2 minimum, Always Use HTTPS on, Browser Integrity Check off (it answers script user agents with error 1010) and the lowest security level, as in Common Practice. Removing a setting restores its earlier value. |
| `TaxKitProductionDnssec` | retained native `Cloudflare.DNS.Dnssec` in `prod` only | Signing active; Cloudflare Registrar publishes the DS record. |
| `TaxKitProductionBotManagement` | retained native `Cloudflare.BotManagement` in `prod` only | Bans no user agent: no Bot Fight Mode, AI-bot, crawler or content-bot blocking, and no Cloudflare-managed robots.txt. |

The graph is one-way: the API is declared first and has no Website address or
binding. Published pages and discovery documents use the fixed Production

Both Workers declare native Cloudflare Workers Cache scoped to their deployed
version: the API with `Cloudflare.cache({ crossVersionCache: false })` in its
native init and the Website with `cache: { enabled: true, crossVersionCache: false }`.
Response headers choose what is public; see the
[frontend](./frontend.md) and [API and SDK](./api-and-sdk.md) owners. Authored
content is an input to both Worker builds (the API bundles the public catalogue;
the Website memo includes the shared packages), so a content-only change
deploys new versions of both and starts new caches. Native gitignore rules do
not reach the memo's `../../packages/**` paths, so the stack names those
excludes itself; without them the hash follows linked `node_modules` into the
package store (about 1.2 million files) and the deploy runs out of memory.

## Observability

Both Workers disable Cloudflare invocation logs, stored logs and traces, because
platform records can include caller URLs. Application diagnostics use fixed
safe fields only; see [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-limit-operational-observations.md).

## Retained analytics project

`alchemy.posthog.run.ts` composes the private infrastructure `./posthog` export.
`TaxKitPostHog/prod` owns one retained `TaxKitProject` identity. The project is
declared only for `prod` and its provider never deletes it. PostHog collection
remains postponed; the app graph references no analytics project. The
[infrastructure guide](../../packages/infrastructure/README.md) owns its details.

## Known limit

The native redirect provider treats a failed read of the zone's shared redirect
ruleset as an empty ruleset, and uploads the Worker before writing the redirect
rule. See the runbook's known limits before another owner adds redirect rules
to the zone.

 *
 * ### Custom Rebuild Scope
 * By default, every non-gitignored file is hashed to decide whether
 * a rebuild is needed. Use `memo` to narrow the scope when your
 * project has large directories that don't affect the build output.
 *
 * **Example:** Narrowing the memo scope
 * ```typescript
 * const site = yield* Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Docs", {
 *   memo: {
 *     include: ["src/**", "content/**", "package.json"],
 *   },
 * });
 * ```
 *
 * **Example:** Rebuilding when a sibling workspace package changes
 * The default scope only hashes files under the project root (plus the
 * nearest lockfile), so edits to a sibling workspace package the app
 * imports do not retrigger the build on their own. Add the sibling's
 * sources with a `../` include glob — and keep `lockfile: true`, since
 * providing `include` otherwise drops the lockfile from the hash:
 * ```typescript
 * const site = yield* Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Web", {
 *   rootDir: "apps/web",
 *   memo: {
 *     include: ["**\/*", "../../packages/env/src/**"],
 *     lockfile: true,
 *   },
 * });
 * ```
 *
 * ### Class Form
 * Calling `Vite` with no arguments returns a constructor you can
 * `extend` to declare the Worker as a named class. The class is both
 * an `Effect` you can `yield*` to deploy and a type you can reference

# Primary Sources and Version Policy

## Version policy

Alchemy and Effect APIs evolve. Before copying any example:

1. inspect the repository's lockfile and installed package version;
2. inspect installed exports and types;
3. consult the matching official documentation;
4. adapt structural examples to that version;
5. add a compile/test check.

Treat examples in this skill as architecture and policy unless they explicitly match the installed version.

## Alchemy

- [Alchemy infrastructure-as-code overview](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/)
- [Stack](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/stack/)
- [Provider](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/provider)
- [Resource lifecycle](https://v2.alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource-lifecycle/)
- [Stages](https://v2.alchemy.run/concepts/stages)
- [Stack concepts](https://v2.alchemy.run/concepts/stack)
- [Provider concepts](https://v2.alchemy.run/concepts/provider)
- [CLI guide](https://v2.alchemy.run/guides/cli)
- [Destroy command](https://alchemy.run/cli/destroy)

## Providers

### Cloudflare website origins

The repository scaffold selects Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81`. Its self URL examples
were checked against that release's source and package types:

- [Worker self URL binding](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/Worker.ts#L1311-L1324)
- [Local self URL resolution](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/LocalWorkerProvider.ts#L1533-L1553)
- [Website.Vite delegates to Worker](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Website/Vite.ts)
- [Deployed self URL resolution](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/WorkerProvider.ts)
- [Native Worker ConfigProvider from resolved bindings](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/WorkerBridge.ts#L295-L311)
- [Deferred self URL accessor and runtime requirement](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/Worker.ts#L1277-L1344)

Recheck these contracts against the selected release when upgrading. These
sources establish address resolution, native configuration support and the
accessor's execution phase. Effect's [pinned configuration sources](../../strict-effect-ts/references/sources.md#native-configuration-and-request-addresses)
establish the application Layer and test-provider pattern. Local source checks
do not prove a deployment or live domain routing.

### Provider documentation

- [Cloudflare Workers API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/workers/)
- [Cloudflare Workers static assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/)
- [Cloudflare Workers observability](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/)
- [Axiom datasets API](https://axiom.co/docs/restapi/endpoints/getDatasets)
- [Axiom OpenTelemetry for Cloudflare Workers](https://axiom.co/docs/guides/opentelemetry-cloudflare-workers)
- [WorkOS redirect URI API](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/redirect-uri)
- [WorkOS redirect URI guidance](https://workos.com/docs/sso/redirect-uris)
- [WorkOS AuthKit API](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit)
- [Vercel deployments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments)
- [Vercel Git deployments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/git)
- [Vercel project configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration)
- [Vercel OIDC](https://vercel.com/docs/oidc)
- [Vercel Observability](https://vercel.com/docs/observability)

- test snapshots;
- error messages.

## Preflight

Run read-only checks before planning or applying:

1. decode stage/source/authority;
2. identify provider account/project/tenant;
3. validate credential class and safe metadata;
4. check quota, entitlement, and capacity;
5. inventory resource identities in scope;
6. verify state backend availability and namespace;
7. detect retained or foreign collisions;
8. verify workflow/environment protection.

Stop on contradictory identity. Do not “best effort” a Production target.

## Plan classification

Normalise the plan into a closed set:

- create;
- update in place;
- replace;
- adopt;

# No-store eviction and version switch caveats — 13 October 2026

The Alchemy Cloudflare cache reference now says a `no-store` reply at a page URL
can evict the stored page even with an identical `Vary` set. It stores
deterministic negotiation answers and permanent redirects publicly as their own
variants, and warns that version-scoped storage is not strict during a switch.
This follows the [shared Vary guidance](2026-10-13-shared-vary-scriptonce.md).

## Evidence

Site DEV-120 Preview, 13 October 2026:

- Before the fix, one fresh `/about` URL gave: plain MISS, plain HIT, then an
  `Accept: text/markdown;q=bad` 406 with `no-store` (BYPASS), then plain MISS.
- After the 400/406 negotiation answers took the page's public policy and
  `Vary: Accept`: page HIT, 406 MISS, page HIT, 406 HIT.
- A request with `Authorization` was answered from the cached page (HIT) and did
  not evict it.

adad Production (`adad.app`), reported by its delivery session:

- Before its fix: page HIT, then a no-store 308 from the legacy host at the same
  path, then page MISS. Matching `Vary: Host` alone did not prevent it.
- After the 308 took the public cache policy: page and redirect each stayed
  HITs in both orders.
- During a later version switch, a reply from the outgoing version stayed
  stored and was served to the new version for over a minute, despite
  `crossVersionCache: false`, until another version replaced it.

Common Practice production and TaxKit production were checked against the
shared `Vary` rule by their own sessions; their records live in those repositories.

## Limits

Cloudflare does not document this eviction behaviour; it is observed hosted
behaviour on 13 October 2026. Each repository must qualify its own pages after
deployment. No starter template generates negotiation code.
