The rules below were checked against Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81` source, with
Common Practice as the reference implementation. Recheck them for the receiving
release.

### Production custom domain

Declare the Production host's domain natively on its Website or Worker:

```typescript
domain: { name: "example.com", redirects: ["www.example.com"] },
workersDev: false,
```

`name` is the canonical host and becomes the Worker's primary `url`. Each
`redirects` host gets its own custom domain for DNS and TLS, plus a rule in the
zone's dynamic redirect phase that answers 301 and keeps path and query. The
rule runs before the Worker, so redirect hosts serve no content. `aliases` are
different: they serve the Worker. Use an alias for an old API host that must
keep answering POST and MCP clients; never turn an API alias into a 301. Do not
build host redirects in Worker code or `ASSETS` rules.

`zoneId` applies to every hostname in the config. Pass it only when all of them
are in that one zone. When hostnames span zones, such as a new apex that also
redirects an old domain, leave it out: native Alchemy looks up each hostname's
zone by name. One shared override would put the other zone's hosts in the
wrong zone.

The zone's redirect ruleset is shared. The native provider replaces only rules
whose description carries its own Worker prefix and passes the rest through.
But it treats a failed read of that ruleset as an empty ruleset, so the next
successful write holds only this Worker's rules and drops rules owned
elsewhere. It also uploads the Worker before writing the rule. Read the zone's
redirect rules before another owner adds one, and record this limit in the
project's runbook.

### workers.dev addresses

`workersDev` controls a Worker's stable `workers.dev` address and a separate
preview address for every uploaded version. The default, `true`, turns on both.

| Website stage | `workersDev`                                | Result                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Production    | `false`                                     | Custom domain only.                          |
| Other stages  | `{ enabled: true, previewsEnabled: false }` | One stable address; no version preview URLs. |

Choose an API Worker's policy separately. Common Practice turns its Production
API address off. With `enabled: false` and previews on, the current version's
preview address becomes the primary `url`; avoid that unless it is the intent.
Each host still binds its own `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`, which resolves to the
custom domain or the stable address. Before turning Production's address off,
check that no Preview, CI check, allowed origin or trace filter still uses it.

### Zone settings, DNSSEC and bot policy

When the project owns its Production zone's edge policy, declare it in the
Production stage only, one retained native resource per concern:

```typescript
const zone = yield* Cloudflare.Zone.Zone("ProductionZone", { name: "example.com" }).pipe(
  adopt(true),
  retain(),
);
yield* Effect.forEach(zoneSettings, ({ resource, settingId, value }) =>
  Cloudflare.Zone.Setting(resource, { zoneId: zone.zoneId, settingId, value }).pipe(retain()),
);
yield* Cloudflare.DNS.Dnssec("ProductionDnssec", {
  zoneId: zone.zoneId,
  status: "active",
}).pipe(retain());
yield* Cloudflare.BotManagement.BotManagement("ProductionBotManagement", {
  zoneId: zone.zoneId,
  fightMode: false,
  aiBotsProtection: "disabled",
  crawlerProtection: "disabled",
  contentBotsProtection: "disabled",
  isRobotsTxtManaged: false,
}).pipe(retain());
```

Keep the reason beside each setting in the project:

| `settingId`        | Value             | Reason                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tls_1_3`          | `on`              | Modern clients negotiate TLS 1.3.                                                                       |
| `min_tls_version`  | `1.2`             | A 1.3 minimum refuses TLS 1.2 clients, including some crawlers.                                         |
| `always_use_https` | `on`              | `http://` requests are redirected instead of served.                                                    |
| `browser_check`    | `off`             | Browser Integrity Check answers default script user agents with Cloudflare error 1010 before the Worker. |
| `security_level`   | `essentially_off` | The fewest IP-reputation challenges for API and agent callers.                                          |

The bot policy above bans no user agent: no Bot Fight Mode, AI-bot blocking,
AI Labyrinth link maze or content-bot blocking, and no Cloudflare-managed
robots.txt prepended to the site's own. It suits API, documentation and
agent-facing sites. Writable bot fields depend on the zone's plan; record and
drop a field the plan rejects rather than work around it.

Lifecycle:

- The zone must already exist. Adopt and retain it; the stack never creates,
  replaces or deletes it.
- Settings, DNSSEC and bot management are per-zone singletons. Alchemy never
  creates or deletes anything physical: it adopts the current value, records it
  as the pre-management value and patches towards the declaration. A first plan
  can still list them as creates.
- The provider's delete restores that pre-management value. `retain()` skips
  the delete, so removing a retained declaration leaves the managed value in
  place. Choose retain or restore deliberately.
- `status: "active"` starts signing, but Cloudflare reports `pending` until the
  parent DS record exists. Cloudflare Registrar publishes it automatically. With
  another registrar, add the resource's `ds` output there; until then the
  status stays `pending`, which is not active. If DNSSEC is already on and no
  state exists, the resource reads as unowned and needs `adopt(true)`.

After apply, check the apex answers 200 and each redirect host answers 301 with
path and query; TLS 1.3 and 1.2 handshakes succeed and TLS 1.1 is refused; a DS
query and a validating resolver confirm DNSSEC; script clients, AI crawlers,
search crawlers and an empty user agent all receive 200; and the settings read
back from Cloudflare equal the declaration.

### Zone token permissions and preflight

Before the first plan that declares these resources, read the zone's current
settings, DNSSEC, bot management and redirect rules with read-only calls and
record them. That record is the "before" for later readback, and it shows
whether the token can read them at all. Planning reads these resources, so a
token without access fails before apply.

The Production token needs these permissions on that zone (Edit in the
dashboard, Write in the API):

| Zone permission       | Needed for                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Zone Settings         | `Cloudflare.Zone.Setting`                                   |
| DNS                   | `Cloudflare.DNS.Dnssec`; Zone Settings alone is refused.    |
| Bot Management        | `Cloudflare.BotManagement`                                  |
| Workers Routes        | Worker custom domains.                                      |
| Dynamic URL Redirects | The zone redirect rules written for `domain.redirects`.     |

Non-Production credentials get no zone access. Widening a token is the owner's
decision. When the owner authorises it, update the existing token in place,
keeping its name, expiry and other policies (for example with
`cf accounts tokens update`). Record the token's permissions and expiry in the
project's deployment runbook, then read the token back before planning.

# Cloudflare zone hosting guidance — 13 October 2026

The Alchemy Cloudflare reference now covers Production custom domains with
native redirects, the `workers.dev` policy, retained zone settings, DNSSEC and
bot policy, the zone token permissions and preflight, monorepo `memo` inputs
and native drift reports. Common Practice is the reference implementation;
TaxKit followed it.

## Evidence

Source behaviour was read in the installed Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81` package:
Worker `domain` and `workersDev` options, the redirect ruleset reconcile (a
failed read becomes an empty ruleset; the Worker uploads first), zone setting,
DNSSEC and bot management singletons and their restore-on-delete, the removal
policy, memo defaults and the drift comparison and command.

Hosted observations, reported by each project's own sessions:

- Common Practice: Browser Integrity Check answered default script user agents
  with error 1010 before the Worker ran; the DNSSEC status stayed `pending`
  until the parent DS record existed; the zone token needed Zone Settings, DNS,
  Bot Management and custom-domain and redirect permissions added.
- TaxKit: a Website `memo` including `../../packages/**` without excludes for
  that tree hashed about 1.21 million files, stalled for six minutes and was
  killed out of memory. `alchemy drift` reported Workers with custom domains
  as changed straight after a clean deploy while `plan` showed no changes.

## Limits

These are guidance and source checks. No starter template changed, and no
deployment was made from this repository. Each project must qualify its own
zone, token and hosted behaviour.
EOF

EOF

diff --git a/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md b/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md
index af4087d..0e540f0 100644
--- a/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md
+++ b/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 - [Routes zones and domains](#routes-zones-and-domains)
 - [Bindings and storage](#bindings-and-storage)
 - [Website origin rules](#website-origin-rules)
+- [Website build inputs in a monorepo](#website-build-inputs-in-a-monorepo)
 - [Secrets](#secrets)
 - [Observability](#observability)
 - [State](#state)
@@ -81,6 +82,154 @@ Treat a zone or domain as foreign unless this repository creates and owns it.
 
 Do not infer route correctness from a Worker URL.
 
+The rules below were checked against Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81` source, with
+Common Practice as the reference implementation. Recheck them for the receiving
+release.
+
+### Production custom domain
+
+Declare the Production host's domain natively on its Website or Worker:
+
+```typescript
+domain: { name: "example.com", redirects: ["www.example.com"] },
+workersDev: false,
+```
+
+`name` is the canonical host and becomes the Worker's primary `url`. Each
+`redirects` host gets its own custom domain for DNS and TLS, plus a rule in the
+zone's dynamic redirect phase that answers 301 and keeps path and query. The
+rule runs before the Worker, so redirect hosts serve no content. `aliases` are
+different: they serve the Worker. Use an alias for an old API host that must
+keep answering POST and MCP clients; never turn an API alias into a 301. Do not
+build host redirects in Worker code or `ASSETS` rules.
+
+`zoneId` applies to every hostname in the config. Pass it only when all of them
+are in that one zone. When hostnames span zones, such as a new apex that also
+redirects an old domain, leave it out: native Alchemy looks up each hostname's
+zone by name. One shared override would put the other zone's hosts in the
+wrong zone.
+
+The zone's redirect ruleset is shared. The native provider replaces only rules
+whose description carries its own Worker prefix and passes the rest through.
+But it treats a failed read of that ruleset as an empty ruleset, so the next
+successful write holds only this Worker's rules and drops rules owned
+elsewhere. It also uploads the Worker before writing the rule. Read the zone's
+redirect rules before another owner adds one, and record this limit in the
+project's runbook.
+
+### workers.dev addresses
+
+`workersDev` controls a Worker's stable `workers.dev` address and a separate
+preview address for every uploaded version. The default, `true`, turns on both.
+
+| Website stage | `workersDev`                                | Result                                       |
+| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
+| Production    | `false`                                     | Custom domain only.                          |
+| Other stages  | `{ enabled: true, previewsEnabled: false }` | One stable address; no version preview URLs. |
+
+Choose an API Worker's policy separately. Common Practice turns its Production
+API address off. With `enabled: false` and previews on, the current version's
+preview address becomes the primary `url`; avoid that unless it is the intent.
+Each host still binds its own `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`, which resolves to the
+custom domain or the stable address. Before turning Production's address off,
+check that no Preview, CI check, allowed origin or trace filter still uses it.
+
+### Zone settings, DNSSEC and bot policy
+
+When the project owns its Production zone's edge policy, declare it in the
+Production stage only, one retained native resource per concern:
+
+```typescript
+// Production only. zoneSettings holds { resource, settingId, value } rows
+// from the table below.
+export const declareZone = Effect.fn("Website.declareZone")(function* () {
+  const zone = yield* Cloudflare.Zone.Zone("ProductionZone", { name: "example.com" }).pipe(
+    adopt(true),
+    retain(),
+  );
+  yield* Effect.forEach(zoneSettings, ({ resource, settingId, value }) =>
+    Cloudflare.Zone.Setting(resource, { zoneId: zone.zoneId, settingId, value }).pipe(retain()),
+  );
+  yield* Cloudflare.DNS.Dnssec("ProductionDnssec", {
+    zoneId: zone.zoneId,
+    status: "active",
+  }).pipe(retain());
+  yield* Cloudflare.BotManagement.BotManagement("ProductionBotManagement", {
+    zoneId: zone.zoneId,
+    fightMode: false,
+    aiBotsProtection: "disabled",
+    crawlerProtection: "disabled",
+    contentBotsProtection: "disabled",
+    isRobotsTxtManaged: false,
+  }).pipe(retain());
+  return zone;
+});
+```
+
+Keep the reason beside each setting in the project:
+
+| `settingId`        | Value             | Reason                                                                                                   |
+| ------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `tls_1_3`          | `on`              | Modern clients negotiate TLS 1.3.                                                                        |
+| `min_tls_version`  | `1.2`             | A 1.3 minimum refuses TLS 1.2 clients, including some crawlers.                                          |
+| `always_use_https` | `on`              | `http://` requests are redirected instead of served.                                                     |
+| `browser_check`    | `off`             | Browser Integrity Check answers default script user agents with Cloudflare error 1010 before the Worker. |
+| `security_level`   | `essentially_off` | The fewest IP-reputation challenges for API and agent callers.                                           |
+
+The bot policy above bans no user agent: no Bot Fight Mode, AI-bot blocking,
+AI Labyrinth link maze or content-bot blocking, and no Cloudflare-managed
+robots.txt prepended to the site's own. It suits API, documentation and
+agent-facing sites. Writable bot fields depend on the zone's plan; record and
+drop a field the plan rejects rather than work around it.
+
+Lifecycle:
+
+- The zone must already exist. Adopt and retain it; the stack never creates,
+  replaces or deletes it.
+- Settings, DNSSEC and bot management are per-zone singletons. Alchemy never
+  creates or deletes anything physical: it adopts the current value, records it
+  as the pre-management value and patches towards the declaration. A first plan
+  can still list them as creates.
+- The provider's delete restores that pre-management value. `retain()` skips
+  the delete, so removing a retained declaration leaves the managed value in
+  place. Choose retain or restore deliberately.
+- `status: "active"` starts signing, but Cloudflare reports `pending` until the
+  parent DS record exists. Cloudflare Registrar publishes it automatically. With
+  another registrar, add the resource's `ds` output there; until then the
+  status stays `pending`, which is not active. If DNSSEC is already on and no
+  state exists, the resource reads as unowned and needs `adopt(true)`.
+
+After apply, check the apex answers 200 and each redirect host answers 301 with
+path and query; TLS 1.3 and 1.2 handshakes succeed and TLS 1.1 is refused; a DS
+query and a validating resolver confirm DNSSEC; script clients, AI crawlers,
+search crawlers and an empty user agent all receive 200; and the settings read
+back from Cloudflare equal the declaration.
+
+### Zone token permissions and preflight

Document Cloudflare zone hosting with native Alchemy

The Cloudflare reference said little about Production hosting: the only
domain guidance was a generic adoption checklist, and the redirect ruleset
limit sat in the State section. Common Practice and TaxKit settled the
pattern, so record it once in the Cloudflare reference, checked against the
installed Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81 source:

- a native custom domain with `www` redirects (301 keeping path and query),
  aliases for serving hosts, `zoneId` only for single-zone configs, and the
  shared redirect ruleset limit;
- the `workers.dev` policy per stage and what the default enables;
- retained zone settings, DNSSEC and bot policy as native singletons, with
  the reason for each value and the retain versus restore choice;
- the zone token permissions and read-only preflight;
- explicit `memo` excludes when an include reaches `../` in a monorepo.

The drift reference now explains why `alchemy drift` can report changes
that `plan` does not, and why plan stays the change gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## What changed

The `alchemy-iac` Cloudflare reference now covers Production hosting with native Alchemy, taking Common Practice as the reference implementation (TaxKit followed it). Each lesson sits in one owner:

- **`references/providers/cloudflare.md`** (under Routes, zones and domains)
  - Production custom domain: native `domain: { name, redirects }` (301 keeping path and query, run before the Worker, so redirect hosts serve no content); `aliases` for hosts that must keep serving, such as an old API; no Worker or `ASSETS` redirect workaround.
  - Pass `zoneId` only when every hostname is in that one zone. Leave it out when hostnames span zones.
  - The shared redirect ruleset limit: a failed read is treated as empty, so a later write can drop rules owned elsewhere, and the Worker is uploaded before the rule is written. Moved here from the State section.
  - `workersDev` per stage: Production Website `false`; other stages `{ enabled: true, previewsEnabled: false }`. The default `true` enables both the stable and version preview addresses. The API policy is chosen separately.
  - Retained zone settings (one `Zone.Setting` each, with reasons, including Browser Integrity Check off because of error 1010), `DNS.Dnssec` active (the Registrar publishes DS; other registrars need the `ds` output added there; `pending` is not active; already-on DNSSEC needs `adopt(true)`), and a `BotManagement` policy that bans no user agent. Singleton lifecycle: these are adopted, never created or deleted. The provider's delete restores the earlier value, but `retain()` skips that delete.
  - Zone token permissions (Zone Settings, DNS for DNSSEC, Bot Management, Workers Routes, Dynamic URL Redirects), a read-only preflight, and in-place token updates made only with the owner's authority.
  - New section on monorepo `memo` inputs: gitignore-derived excludes do not cover `../` includes, setting `exclude` replaces those defaults, and `include`/`exclude` drop the lockfile unless `lockfile: true` is set. Name excludes for both trees.
- **`references/operations/adoption-drift-recovery-and-destroy.md`**: native `alchemy drift` compares a fresh provider read with saved attributes while `plan` compares the declaration with saved props. Drift exits successfully even when it reports changes. Plan stays the change gate, and `--repair` is not a substitute for an authorised apply.
- **`references/sources.md`**: pinned beta.81 sources for each source-checked claim.
- Archive record of the source checks and hosted observations, a patch Changeset and refreshed `sources.json` fingerprints.

## Checks

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- `bun run source:sync`
- `bun run test`: passed (37 + 14 skill tests, CLI 14, tooling 62; 8/8 Turbo tasks)
- `bun run verification`: passed (format, lint, types, knip, build, manifest, distribution and source checks)

## Not checked

- No deployment, provider call or token change was made. The hosted observations (error 1010, the memo stall, drift reports and DNSSEC `pending`) come from the Common Practice and TaxKit sessions.
- No starter template changed. The repository starter's API Worker still declares `workersDev: true`, which also enables version preview addresses. Changing it needs the template render qualification.
- Not released. The Version Packages PR will consume the Changeset.

EOF

content.text:
I've opened PR https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/pull/55 (branch `claude/cloudflare-zone-hosting-guidance`, made from `origin/main` in the worktree `/private/tmp/commonplace-zone-hosting`). It is not merged or released. The checks passed: `bun run test` and `bun run verification`.

**Files changed**
- `plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md`: four new subsections under "Routes, zones, and domains" (custom domain, `workers.dev`, zone settings/DNSSEC/bot policy, token permissions and preflight) and a new "Website build inputs in a monorepo" section. The redirect-limit sentence that sat in the State section was removed, because the domain section now owns it.
- `plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/operations/adoption-drift-recovery-and-destroy.md`: one paragraph on native `alchemy drift`.
- `plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/references/sources.md`: links to the beta.81 Alchemy source behind each claim.
- `plugins/development-workflows/sources.json`: fingerprints refreshed with `source:sync`.
- `.changeset/cloudflare-zone-hosting.md`: a patch Changeset. The changelog and version are left to the Version Packages PR, as the release runbook requires.
- `docs/archive/scaffold-qualification/2026-10-13-zone-hosting.md` and `docs/archive/README.md`: an evidence record, following the pattern of the previous change.
- `SKILL.md` is unchanged. Its existing "load the Cloudflare reference" step already leads there, so a pointer would only repeat it.

**What was missing or contradictory before**
- **Custom domains:** nothing on `domain.redirects` versus `aliases`, or on when to pass `zoneId`. The redirect ruleset limit was only hinted at, in the State section and a table in `native-migrations.md`.
- **`workers.dev`:** no policy at all. Nothing said that the default `true` also turns on a preview address for every version.
- **Zone resources:** zone settings, DNSSEC and bot management weren't covered. That includes the singleton lifecycle, the `pending` DS trap, and the fact that `retain()` skips the provider's restore.
- **Token permissions:** no zone permission list. The read-only preflight was only a generic checklist.
- **`memo`:** only "include content in memo inputs", with no warning about `../` paths.
- **Drift:** nothing on native `alchemy drift` disagreeing with `plan`, its successful exit even when it reports changes, or `--repair`.

**Checked against the installed beta.81 source**
- All six lessons hold.
- A failed read of the zone's redirect rules really is treated as empty, and the Worker is uploaded before the redirect rule is written.
- Setting `exclude` replaces the gitignore defaults entirely, and setting `include` or `exclude` drops the lockfile unless `lockfile: true` is set.
- Drift compares a fresh provider read with the attributes saved at the last deploy, while plan compares the declaration with saved props. That explains why drift can report changes when plan shows none.
- One new finding: if DNSSEC is already on and Alchemy has no state for it, the resource reads as unowned and needs `adopt(true)`. Neither reference project hit this because both zones started unsigned.

**Two problems outside this repo**
1. TaxKit's `docs/architecture/deployment.md` says "Removing a setting restores its earlier value". That's wrong because TaxKit retains its settings, and `retain()` skips the restore. I didn't edit it, since TaxKit was read-only for this task.
2. The repository starter's API Worker (`skills/repo-structure/assets/repository/apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts.tmpl`) still sets `workersDev: true`, which turns on version preview addresses. Changing a template needs its own render qualification, so I've listed it in the PR under "Not checked" rather than changing it.

**Not verified here:** the hosted observations (error 1010, the memo out-of-memory stall, the drift reports, DNSSEC staying `pending`) come from the Common Practice and TaxKit sessions. I made no deployment, provider call or token change.
